newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian stocks up, led by bluechips.
newsitem.headline: Colombian stocks up, led by bluechips.

text.p: Colombian stocks rose Wednesday driven by foreign fund and local investor interest in bluechips.

Bogota's IBB index closed up 1.02 percent at 1,196.06 amid a 3.8 billion volume while Medellin's IBOMED general price index gained 0.65 percent to close at 17,953.07 amid a 4.8 billion peso trade. "There was strong demand from local investors and foreign funds after a week of virtual apathy," a trader said.

One of the day's biggest gainers was insurance giant Suramericana de Seguros, part of the powerful Sindicato Antioqueno group. It was up 2.43 percent to 29,500 in Bogota and remained unchanged at the same price in Medellin.
Banco de Bogota, head of Luis Carlos Sarmiento's financial empire, was up 1.22 percent to 7,000 in Bogota and up 1.21 percent to 6,998.99 in Medellin.
"Funds bought shares at high prices because they're confident of good second half results. There's a positive mood," another Bogota broker said.
Cementos del Caribe, also part of the Sindicato Antioqueno, was up 1.41 percent to 5,801 in Bogota and up 2.09 percent to 5,850 in Medellin.
Brewing giant Bavaria BAV.BGu BAV.MLu, head of the Santo Domingo industrial empire, gained 0.85 percent to close at 8,119 in Bogota and was up 0.64 percent to 8,115 in Medellin.

Bancoquia bank BCA.BG, which signed a deal to sell a 55 percent stake in the bank to Spain's Banco Santander earlier this month, rose 1.14 percent to 3,100 in Bogota and remained unchanged at 3,080.1 in Medellin.
Cement manufacturer Cemento Argos, the country's largest cement company, was up 1.12 percent to 9,000 in Bogota and gained 0.55 percent to close at the same price in Medellin.
